This version follows the updates I made for the ergm tutorial at IBS at CU in 2018.
I've extracted only the steps for the pertinent visualizations used here.

``` {r setup, echo=F, warning=F, message=F}
##########################################################################
#	0.1 	Setting up your R environment
##########################################################################
# This is the wrapper package-suite (along w/ its dependencies) we're using for analyses and visualizations here.
#install.packages("statnet")			# The first time you install a package
library(statnet)						      # Attach the library to your session

# These 2 are merely to present some of the results in more readable graphics (code works w/o)
#install.packages("coda")
library(coda)
#install.packages("latticeExtra")
library(latticeExtra)

##########################################################################
#	0.2 	Loading our data
##########################################################################
# Chris Marcum produced a single R environment w/ a # of datasets
# https://github.com/cmarcum/TVHookupNetworks/blob/master/TvContacts.Rdata
greys <- readRDS("data/greys.rds")

# Greys Anatomy data come from: Lind, B. 2012. Bad Hessian Blog. https://goo.gl/oJsZpH

mg <- 206-555-0199 # Reportedly Meredith Grey's phone number (for seed setting)
```

``` {r model, include=T}
##########################################################################
#	1. 	Exploratory visualization of the data
##########################################################################
la <- plot(greys)		#fix plot coordinates, so they don't jump around if we re-plot later
plot(greys, coord=la, 
     vertex.col=get.vertex.attribute(greys, "nrace"), 	
     label=get.vertex.attribute(greys, "name"), 
     label.cex=0.4,                    
     vertex.sides=(50*(get.vertex.attribute(greys, "sex")=="F")+4), #circles & squares 	
     vertex.cex=.05*(2013-get.vertex.attribute(greys, "birthyear")))	


##########################################################################
#	2.  Fit an ergm
##########################################################################
# Here, we're building a model that only has terms for:
      # (1) gender homophily, 
      # (2) age similarity, & 
      # (3) an avoidance of isolates
# Note that this is only the best fitting model, according to diagnostics, etc. For a more formal fitting process/exercise, see Lind's original post, or a more complete ergm tutorial.

set.seed(mg) # fixing model estimate starting point
gr.het_noisol_age<-ergm(greys~edges+nodematch("sex")+degree(1)+absdiff("birthyear"), control=control.ergm(MCMC.burnin=50000, MCMC.interval=5000))
gr.het_noisol_age.gof<-gof(gr.het_noisol_age)			# Estimating Goodness of Fit with default set of diagnostics
summary(gr.het_noisol_age.gof) 						# Summarize the goodness of fit
par(mfrow=c(1,3)); plot(gr.het_noisol_age.gof)
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
summary(gr.het_noisol_age) 							# Summarize the model
mcmc.diagnostics(gr.het_noisol_age)

##########################################################################
# 3.  Pick a plot
##########################################################################
# Let's start by creating 100 simulation draws to choose from (likely overkill).
set.seed(mg) # fixing sample draws
gr.nisol.het.aged.sim <- simulate(gr.het_noisol_age, nsim=100)

# Looping to find a draw w/ at least one isolate AND one same-sex pair (to demonstrate stochasticity).
# for(i in 1:20){
# plot(gr.nisol.het.aged.sim[[i]],
#      vertex.col=(get.vertex.attribute(gr.nisol.het.aged.sim[[i]], "sex")=="F")+1,
#      vertex.cex=.05*(2013-get.vertex.attribute(gr.nisol.het.aged.sim[[i]], "birthyear")))
# }

 i<-1 # this one worked
```

```{r plot}
##########################################################################
# 4.  Generate included plot
##########################################################################
plot(gr.nisol.het.aged.sim[[i]], 
      vertex.col=(get.vertex.attribute(gr.nisol.het.aged.sim[[i]], "sex")=="F")+1, 	
      vertex.cex=.05*(2013-get.vertex.attribute(gr.nisol.het.aged.sim[[i]], "birthyear")))
```
